review.scope: Nineteen exact defect/control pairs across fourteen synthetic and five pinned public repository groups. ARC001: a three-layer Python package whose route layer imports the model layer directly (one unsupported_syntax Python case is excluded from ratios). PSR005 (spec 094): a Spec Kit-installed skill edited after install. PSR006 (spec 099): a scaffolder template AGENTS.md below templates/<app>/files/. PSR007 (spec 100 stage 3): one command kept under two agent roots with a line changed; the control holds identical copies, a shared basename and two renderings of a generated file. PSR008: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md sharing all but one line; the control a pointer and a different document. STR004 (spec 100): a package AGENTS.md over a 200 byte chain budget; a template AGENTS.md is not counted. STR008: a backup copy of a document in a documentation directory.
review.methodology: Labels were authored from pinned source and seeded mutations before DocGuard output was reviewed. The ARC001 pair (2026-09-18), the PSR005 pairs (2026-11-12), the PSR006 pair and the STR004 pair (2026-11-13) were authored labels-first and matched their labels on the first run, except that the PSR005 evaluation pair first abstained until an early return in Path-Scoped-Rules was fixed. The STR004 control fails on the code before spec 100, where the template chain was counted. The STR008 pair (2026-11-13) was authored labels-first and matched on the first run. The PSR007 and PSR008 pairs (2026-11-13) were authored labels-first, and the run was repeated with --external, where the 36 earlier cases matched their recorded results on these detectors; the PSR007 control first abstained because the fixture held nothing else Path-Scoped-Rules examines, and a pointer was added to it.
review.limitations: Finite scoped cases do not establish exhaustive documentation or detector correctness. Thirteen of the tool’s finding codes are measured here; the rest carry no benchmark evidence. ARC001, PSR006, PSR007, PSR008, STR004 and STR008 are each measured by a single defect/control pair in one repository group, so each point estimate is below the reporting floor and backs off to the whole-corpus tier. PSR008 has no positive example in the 21 real repositories surveyed (no two root instruction files share more than 13% of their lines), so its pair measures the detector, not its rate on real files.
review.caveat: Benchmark precision on a deliberately balanced corpus of 20 defect and 20 clean-control cases across 20 repository groups and 20 causal families. This is DocGuard's precision on labelled cases, not the probability that a finding in your repository is real; quote every ratio with its n and Wilson 95% bound.
